extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) staff, OPLA, patent owners and practitioners involved in ex parte/inter partes reexamination, reissue, and interference proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for handling multiple reexamination requests, merged reexamination/reissue proceedings, and copending interference matters; guidance for deciding, implementing, and administrating mergers and related filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fast processing and assignment of second reexamination request
rubrics_metrics.description: The second request (Request 2) should be processed as quickly as possible and assigned to the same examiner to whom the first request (Request 1) is assigned. Request 2 should be decided immediately without waiting the usual period (e.g., for submission of art).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Request 2 is denied, ex parte prosecution of Request 1 should continue. If Request 2 is granted, mail the order immediately. Request 2 should be determined on its own merits and should not rely on or refer to the decision issued in Request 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold merged requests pending patent owner statement/reply
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon grant of Request 2, the two requests should be held in storage until the patent owner’s statement and any reply by the requester have been received in Request 2, or until the time for filing same expires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After receipt and processing of the statement/reply or expiration of the filing time, the CRU Director or delegate prepares a decision whether to merge the proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to merge issued by CRU Director (or delegate)
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision whether to merge the reexamination proceedings is made by the CRU Director (or the CRU Director’s delegate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions on the merits of petitions to merge multiple reexamination proceedings will be made by the CRU Director (or to the CRU SPE if delegated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to maintain identical claims in merged files
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision by the CRU Director to merge the reexamination proceedings should include a requirement that the patent owner maintain identical claims in both files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The maintenance of identical amendments in the files is required as long as the reexamination proceedings remain merged. If identical amendments are not present at the time merger is ordered, the patent owner will be required to submit an appropriate 'housekeeping' amendment placing the same amendments in the proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-response filing format for merged proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Responses by the patent owner, and any other paper filed in the merged proceeding, must consist of a single response, addressed to both files, filed in duplicate, each bearing a signature and containing identifying data for both files, for entry in both files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both files will be maintained as separate complete files even though a single response is submitted for both.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-month period to make claims identical when merger ordered
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the claims are not the same in both files, the decision of merger will indicate that the patent owner is given 1 month to provide an amendment to make the claims the same in each file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identical amendments are to be placed in all files; CRU will await submission of the amendment or the expiration of the time to submit the amendment. After amendment is received and processed or time expires, the merged proceeding will be returned to the examiner to issue an Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to timely submit required identical amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment to make the claims the same in each file is required by the merger decision but is not timely submitted, any claim that does not contain identical text in all of the merged proceedings should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, as being indefinite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such claims are treated as failing to particularly point out the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner should issue Office action at most advanced point of first proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the merged proceeding is returned to the examiner for issuance of an Office action, the examiner should prepare an Office action at the most advanced point possible for the first proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if the first proceeding is ready for a final rejection and the second proceeding does not provide any new information calling for a new ground of rejection, the examiner should issue a final rejection for the merged proceeding using prosecution-stage guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing when ex parte prosecution has not begun in Request 1
rubrics_metrics.description: If the ex parte prosecution stage has not yet begun in Request 1 when Request 2 is received, Request 1 should be processed to the point where it is ready for ex parte prosecution and then normally held until Request 2 is granted and ready for ex parte action following the statement and reply; thereafter, the two proceedings would be merged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Request 2 is denied, there will be no merger and prosecution continues solely on Request 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single combined examiner action and file-identifying requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When prosecution is appropriate in merged proceedings, a single combined examiner’s action will be prepared. Each action will contain the control number of the two proceedings on every page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single action cover form (having both control numbers penned in at the top) is provided; clerical staff copy the action cover form and use the PALM printer to print appropriate data on original and copy. Each requester and the patent owner receive copies and cover forms; place PTOL-465 on top of the package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of Notices of Intent to Issue Reexamination Certificate (NIRC) in merged files
rubrics_metrics.description: When a NIRC is appropriate, plural notices will be printed and both reexamination files will be processed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The TC or CRU should prepare the file of concurrent proceedings as specified in MPEP § 2287 before release to Office of Data Management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines extend to more than two copending requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The above guidelines should be extended to those situations where more than two requests for reexamination are filed for a single patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the same merger, filing, and processing mechanics when multiple (>2) requests are involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy against merging when second request unduly delays first proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: If a second request for reexamination will unduly delay the first reexamination proceeding, the two proceedings generally will not be merged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: merging should not delay prosecution and must be consistent with the statutory 'special dispatch' requirement of 35 U.S.C. 305. The Office retains authority to merge where efficiency and special dispatch are served; decisions are case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-fee rule in merged proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the proceedings have been merged and a paper is filed which requires payment of a fee (e.g., excess claim fee, extension of time, petition fee, appeal fee, brief fee, oral hearing fee), only a single fee need be paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: only one fee need be paid for an appeal brief even though copies must be filed for each file in the merged proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: No premature petitions to merge — returned if filed before order to reexamine
rubrics_metrics.description: No petition to merge multiple reexamination proceedings is necessary since the Office will generally sua sponte decide; any petition to merge filed prior to the determination (37 CFR 1.515) and order to reexamine (37 CFR 1.525) on the second request will not be considered and will be returned by the CRU Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision returning such a premature petition will be made of record in both reexamination files, but no copy of the petition will be retained by the Office. Patent owners may file a petition to merge after the order to reexamine (and are advised to include it with the patent owner’s statement under 37 CFR 1.530).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may properly petition to merge and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner can file a petition to merge the proceedings at any time after the order to reexamine; a requester who is not the patent owner may petition to merge as part of a reply under 37 CFR 1.535 if the CRU Director has not acted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition to merge filed by a party other than the patent owner or one of the requesters is improper under 37 CFR 1.550(g) and will be returned to that party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory notification of concurrent proceedings (37 CFR 1.565 / 41.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: In an ex parte reexamination proceeding, the patent owner must inform the Office of any prior or concurrent proceedings in which the patent is or was involved (interferences, reissues, reexaminations, litigation) and the results. Under 37 CFR 41.8(a), parties must identify real party-in-interest and each judicial/administrative proceeding that could affect the Board proceeding within 20 days of change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These notifications are designed to keep the Office and parties informed and to eliminate procedural surprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination generally not delayed or stayed because of interference
rubrics_metrics.description: The general policy of the Office is that a reexamination proceeding will not be delayed, or stayed, because of an interference or the possibility of an interference, due to the requirement of 35 U.S.C. 305 for 'special dispatch'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will make required decisions in the reexamination and go forward with interference to the extent desirable; the Board may tailor specific solutions where proceedings are copending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination proceeding cannot itself be an interference
rubrics_metrics.description: Although a patent being reexamined may become involved in an interference with an application, the reexamination proceeding itself can never be involved in an interference proceeding (because an interference relates to applications or patents, not proceedings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See statutory basis (35 U.S.C. 135) — reexamination is neither an application nor a patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when applicant attempts to provoke an interference with patent under reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: When an amendment is filed in a pending application seeking to provoke an interference with a patent involved in a reexamination proceeding, the applicant must comply with 37 CFR 41.202(a), including identifying the patent under reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponding application claims may be rejected on applicable grounds including prior art cited in reexamination. Examiner must notify OPLA before proposing the interference; an interference may not be proposed unless authorized by OPLA. If interference not authorized, further action on the application should be suspended until the reexamination certificate has been issued and published. Form paragraph 23.16 may be used to notify applicant of suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion/request to suspend interference pending reexamination (41.121(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A miscellaneous motion under 37 CFR 41.121(a)(3) to suspend an interference pending the outcome of a reexamination proceeding may be made at any time during the interference by any party thereto; the motion must be presented to the administrative patent judge (APJ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension is not favored; normally no consideration until a reexamination order is issued and motions in the interference disposed of. If denied by the APJ, a request to stay may be made to the Director under 37 CFR 1.565(e). A request to stay under 1.565(e) will be decided by the Chief APJ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to Board when reexamination request filed during interference
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 41.8(a), the patent owner must notify the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences that a request for reexamination was filed, within 20 days of receiving notice of the request having been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent owner files the request, the 20 days run from the filing date. Such requests will be processed normally; no delay of reexamination because requester is not a party to the interference. If examiner orders reexamination and subsequently rejects a patent claim corresponding to a count in the interference, the attention of the Board shall be called thereto.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file notice of interference in reexamination when interference declared
rubrics_metrics.description: When the patent being reexamined becomes involved in an interference, the patent owner is required to file in the reexamination proceeding a paper giving notice of the interference proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This and related requirements are designed to keep the Office and parties informed and to eliminate procedural surprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to stay reexamination because of interference — timing and proper parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition to stay a reexamination proceeding because of an interference filed prior to the determination (37 CFR 1.515) and order to reexamine (37 CFR 1.525) will not be considered and will be returned; a petition may be filed by the patent owner as part of the patent owner’s statement under 37 CFR 1.530 or thereafter. A party to the interference who is also a requester may petition as part of a reply under 37 CFR 1.535. Improper petitions by others are returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Premature petitions returned by CRU or TC Director; petitions filed subsequent to the order are referred to OPLA for decision; all merits decisions on petitions to stay are made in OPLA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board notification and action after issuance of reexamination certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: If one or more claims of a patent involved in an interference are canceled or amended by issuance and publication of a reexamination certificate, the Board must be promptly notified; the patent owner must notify the administrative patent judge upon issuance and publication of the certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt notification ensures appropriate interference action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy and mechanics for merging reissue applications with reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reissue application and an ex parte reexamination proceeding on which an order pursuant to § 1.525 has been mailed are pending concurrently on a patent, a decision will usually be made to merge the two proceedings or to suspend one of the two proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where merger is ordered, the merged examination will be conducted in accordance with §§ 1.171–1.179, and the patent owner will be required to place and maintain the same claims in the reissue application and the ex parte reexamination proceeding during the pendency of the merged proceeding. Examiner's actions and patent owner responses apply to both proceedings and must be physically entered into both files. Any ex parte reexamination proceeding merged with a reissue application shall be concluded by the grant of the reissued patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification duty when reissue application and reexamination are concurrent
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a reissue application and a reexamination proceeding are pending concurrently, the patent owner (reissue applicant) has the responsibility to notify the Office of such via a Notification of Concurrent Proceedings in the reissue application (37 CFR 1.178(b)) and in the reexamination proceeding (37 CFR 1.565(a) or 1.985) as early as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify OPLA promptly and hand-deliver paper files if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for decision on merger/stay for reissue and reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision whether to merge the reissue application examination and the ex parte reexamination proceeding, or to stay one proceeding, will not be made prior to the mailing of an order to reexamine (37 CFR 1.525) and the expiration of the statement-reply period following the order to reexamine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Until decision mailed, the two proceedings continue simultaneously but separately. Determination on a reexamination request must not be delayed because of a copending reissue application (35 U.S.C. 304 and 37 CFR 1.515 require a determination within 3 months of the filing date of the request).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors considered in deciding whether to merge or stay reissue/reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision to merge or not merge is within the sole discretion of the Office and is made case-by-case based upon the status of the various proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider status of reissue application examination (e.g., whether on appeal), status of reexamination (e.g., on appeal or NIRC issued), whether reissue raises issues not proper for reexamination, and whether merger would expedite conduct of proceedings. Precedent cases (In re Onda, Stoddard, Scragg) may be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment when reissue will issue before determination on reexam request
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reissue patent will issue before the determination on the reexamination request must be made, the determination should normally be delayed until after granting of the reissue patent and then made on the basis of the claims in the reissue patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination, if ordered, would then be on reissue patent claims rather than original patent claims. Reissue claims used as starting point must be presented as a 'clean copy' in the reexamination proceeding (bracketed/italic formatting removed as required). Form paragraph 22.05 may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: When reissue exam progressed such that merger is not desirable — stay & shortened response periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the reissue application examination has progressed to a point where merger of the two proceedings is not desirable at that time, the reexamination will generally be stayed until reissue examination is complete on the issues then pending. After stay removed, if proceedings are merged or reexam conducted separately as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a stay of reexamination is removed following reissue application examination, the first Office action will set a shortened statutory period for response of 1 month (unless longer warranted); the second Office action will normally be final and also have a 1-month period. Shortened periods prevent undue delay and support 'special dispatch'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner assignment and conduct for merged reissue/reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to the appropriate examiner assignment of the merged reexamination/reissue proceeding, see MPEP § 2236. Examiner actions and patent owner responses in a merged proceeding apply to both the reissue application and the ex parte reexamination proceeding and will be physically entered into both files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proper assignment and entry mechanics consistent with merged-file processing.
